result.reason: B is clearer: section headings let the reader navigate, the benchmark is explained in plain language ("global stocks and US bonds held at our glide path target weights"), and the fee change is framed as the result of the clients' own request rather than an internal mechanic. A buries five performance figures in one undifferentiated paragraph and leaves "comparison index," "glide path step," and "breakpoint purposes" unexplained, with a passive fee paragraph that obscures the simple fact that the fee is dropping. B also wins on tone, which turns on the tone-note requirement to answer Nils's May question directly. A only gestures at it ("aligns with your question in May regarding whether a higher equity allocation was appropriate"), acknowledging without answering. B names Nils, validates the question, and gives two concrete reassurances: the equity target steps down automatically each year, and the first-year tuition money is already out of equities in maturity-matched 2031 Treasuries. B's register — warm, direct, closing with an invitation to call — suits parents planning for a 13-year-old, whereas A's "your son Mateo's education portfolio" and generic offer to "discuss your financial goals further" read as form-letter. Both carry the UTMA disclosure verbatim and neither mentions the internal-only leave. A is competent and sendable after revision; B needs none. Judgment is on clarity and tone only, not length or factual accuracy.
